pull_request.body:
Fixes #14403.

## Cause
`applyOldStringEdit` converts the replacement to the file's line ending only on its fuzzy paths and when `matchLineEndings` rewrites old/new together. When `old_string` matches the file literally, both literal branches (single match and `replace_all`) wrote `new_string` verbatim, so a multi-line replacement put bare LF into a CRLF file while the tool reported success. `edit_file`, `multi_edit` and the preview share this function.

## Blast radius
`internal/tools/builtin/encoding_helpers.go` only: the two literal branches now go through `replaceLiteral`, which gives each replacement the line ending of the line it lands in (its own newline, or the previous line's when it is the last, unterminated line). The fuzzy paths, `matchLineEndings`, encoding handling and the empty-`old` behaviour are unchanged, and the receipt now records the replacement as actually written. I chose the per-line ending over the file-level rule the fuzzy path uses because a file-level rule would put CR into an LF region of a mixed file.

## Neighbouring behaviours tested
New table test for single match, `replace_all`, no trailing newline, LF file, mixed file (both regions, and `replace_all` across both), a replacement already using CRLF (not doubled) and a replacement with no break; an `edit_file` test with the exact CRLF fixture from the report. The full `internal/tools/...` suite, repolint and golangci-lint pass; the new tests fail on the old code (5 of 9 cases and the `edit_file` one) and pass now.

## Why this layer
The shared edit function owns the replacement text for all three callers, so the fix is one helper there instead of per-tool conversion.
